claim: After six generations of backcrossing, the survival of Rab23-/- homozygote embryos was prolonged to E18.5.
source: After six generations, the survival of the Rab23-/- homozygote embryos were prolonged to E18.5, and this allowed us to study skeletal development of these mice.
evidence: This is a methodological claim describing the experimental outcome.

claim: Rab23-/- mice at E18.5 exhibited craniosynostosis in the coronal suture.
source: Rab23-/- mice at embryonic day E18.5 exhibited craniosynostosis in the coronal, parietal-temporal, fronto-nasal and in the lambdoid sutures when compared to their wild type (Wt) littermates (Figure 1A–E).
evidence: This is supported by µ-CT and skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Rab23-/- mice at E18.5 exhibited craniosynostosis in the parietal-temporal suture.
source: Rab23-/- mice at embryonic day E18.5 exhibited craniosynostosis in the coronal, parietal-temporal, fronto-nasal and in the lambdoid sutures when compared to their wild type (Wt) littermates (Figure 1A–E).
evidence: This is supported by µ-CT and skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Rab23-/- mice at E18.5 exhibited craniosynostosis in the fronto-nasal suture.
source: Rab23-/- mice at embryonic day E18.5 exhibited craniosynostosis in the coronal, parietal-temporal, fronto-nasal and in the lambdoid sutures when compared to their wild type (Wt) littermates (Figure 1A–E).
evidence: This is supported by µ-CT and skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Rab23-/- mice at E18.5 exhibited craniosynostosis in the lambdoid suture.
source: Rab23-/- mice at embryonic day E18.5 exhibited craniosynostosis in the coronal, parietal-temporal, fronto-nasal and in the lambdoid sutures when compared to their wild type (Wt) littermates (Figure 1A–E).
evidence: This is supported by µ-CT and skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Only parieto-temporal sutures showed bi-lateral suture fusion (100%) in all Rab23-/- samples.
source: The prevalence of premature suture fusion in Rab23-/- mice represented as percentage and only parieto-temporal sutures showed bi-lateral suture fusion (100%) in all the samples (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Rab23-/- mice showed pre-axial polydactyly (seven digits) of the forelimb.
source: Rab23-/- mice showed pre-axial polydactyly (seven digits) of the forelimb and preaxial polysyndactyly (seven digits) of the hindlimbs (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Rab23-/- mice showed preaxial polysyndactyly (seven digits) of the hindlimbs.
source: Rab23-/- mice showed pre-axial polydactyly (seven digits) of the forelimb and preaxial polysyndactyly (seven digits) of the hindlimbs (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by skeletal staining data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Polydactyly and craniosynostosis were observed (100%) in all Rab23-/- samples examined.
source: Polydactyly and craniosynostosis were observed (100%) in all Rab23-/- samples examined.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the experimental data.

claim: At E18.5, 5% of Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures exhibited unilateral suture fusion.
source: At E18.5, 5% of Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures exhibited unilateral suture fusion (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Unfused Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures showed abnormal bony protrusions from parietal bones toward interparietal bone.
source: Compared to Wt samples (Figure 1I), unfused Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures showed abnormal bony protrusions from parietal bones toward interparietal bone (Figure 1J) or ectopic bones in the lambdoid suture (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is supported by µ-CT data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: Unfused Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures showed ectopic bones in the lambdoid suture.
source: Compared to Wt samples (Figure 1I), unfused Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures showed abnormal bony protrusions from parietal bones toward interparietal bone (Figure 1J) or ectopic bones in the lambdoid suture (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is supported by µ-CT data shown in Figure 1K.

claim: At E18.5, Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures were narrower than Wt lambdoid sutures.
source: At this stage, Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures were narrower than Wt lambdoid sutures (Figure 1L).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 1L.

claim: 95% of Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures were consistently patent at E18.5.
source: As 95% of Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures were consistently patent at E18.5 they were chosen as a model to study the role of RAB23 in osteogenesis.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the experimental data.

claim: Rab23-/- mice die neonatally.
source: Rab23-/- mice die neonatally, therefore, analysis of Rab23-/- lambdoid suture beyond the E18.5 stage was assessed by in vitro calvarial explant culture (Rice et al., 2003b; Figure 1M).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental work.

claim: Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures fused predictably after 3 days of in vitro culture.
source: Wt and patent Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures harvested for culture at E18.5, Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures fused predictably after 3 days of culture (Figure 1N,O).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro culture data shown in Figure 1N,O.

claim: Rab23 was expressed in suture mesenchyme with the strongest signal in interfrontal, sagittal and coronal sutures and parietal bone side of the lambdoid suture.
source: Rab23 was expressed in suture mesenchyme with the strongest signal in interfrontal, sagittal and coronal sutures and parietal bone side of the lambdoid suture (Figure 1P–a).
evidence: This is supported by whole-mount in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1P-a.

claim: Rab23 expression was found in the osteogenic fronts of the calvarial sutures and throughout the sutural mesenchyme.
source: Analysis of tissue sections revealed Rab23 expression in the osteogenic fronts of the calvarial sutures and throughout the sutural mesenchyme (Figure 1P–b).
evidence: This is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1P-b.

claim: RAB23 was expressed in the lambdoid sutural osteogenic fronts and in the underlying cartilage.
source: RAB23 was expressed in the lambdoid sutural osteogenic fronts and in the underlying cartilage.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical staining data.

claim: RAB23 co-expressed with RUNX2 in the osteogenic front.
source: Co-expression with RUNX2 confirmed the cells in the osteogenic front to be osteoprogenitor or osteoblast (Figure 1P–c).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical staining data shown in Figure 1P-c.

claim: RAB23 protein is present in the suture at E15.5.
source: Western blotting of proteins extracted from E15.5 Wt calvarial frontal, sagittal and lambdoid sutures along with their osteogenic fronts confirmed the presence of RAB23 protein in the suture (Figure 1P–d).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 1P-d.

claim: A microarray-based gene expression analysis of whole Wt and Rab23-/- calvaria samples at E15.5 was performed.
source: To investigate differentially expressed genes between Wt and Rab23-/- calvaria and to find candidate genes responsible for the craniosynostosis in the RAB23-deficient mice, we performed a microarray-based gene expression analysis of whole Wt and Rab23-/- calvaria samples excluding the skin and underlying brain at E15.5 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a methodological claim describing the experimental approach.

claim: 223 genes were significantly differentially expressed between Wt and Rab23-/- calvaria.
source: Our analysis revealed 223 significantly differentially expressed genes between the Wt and Rab23-/- calvaria (t-test, p<0.05) (Figure 2B, Supplementary file 1, MIAME-compliant data has been deposited in GEO database as source data, GEO accession GSE140884).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data shown in Figure 2B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: 115 genes were upregulated in Rab23-/- calvaria compared to Wt.
source: Among these genes, 115 genes were upregulated (Figure 2B, red) and 108 genes were downregulated (Figure 2B, green).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 108 genes were downregulated in Rab23-/- calvaria compared to Wt.
source: Among these genes, 115 genes were upregulated (Figure 2B, red) and 108 genes were downregulated (Figure 2B, green).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Fgf10 was found to be overexpressed in the microarray in Rab23-/- calvaria.
source: Fgf10 was found to be overexpressed in the microarray in Rab23-/- calvaria (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Fgf10 has been shown to be expressed early in calvarial development.
source: Fgf10 was selected as a candidate for further analysis as it has previously been shown to be expressed early in calvarial development and has been implicated in craniosynostosis pathogenesis (Hajihosseini et al., 2009; Veistinen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Fgf10 has been implicated in craniosynostosis pathogenesis.
source: Fgf10 was selected as a candidate for further analysis as it has previously been shown to be expressed early in calvarial development and has been implicated in craniosynostosis pathogenesis (Hajihosseini et al., 2009; Veistinen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Fgf10 expression was elevated in whole calvarial mesenchyme at E15.5.
source: Fgf10 expression was elevated in whole calvarial mesenchyme, lambdoid sutural mesenchymal tissue and in calvaria derived (CD) mesenchymal cells at E15.5 as assessed by RT-qPCR (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Fgf10 expression was elevated in lambdoid sutural mesenchymal tissue at E15.5.
source: Fgf10 expression was elevated in whole calvarial mesenchyme, lambdoid sutural mesenchymal tissue and in calvaria derived (CD) mesenchymal cells at E15.5 as assessed by RT-qPCR (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Fgf10 expression was elevated in calvaria derived mesenchymal cells at E15.5.
source: Fgf10 expression was elevated in whole calvarial mesenchyme, lambdoid sutural mesenchymal tissue and in calvaria derived (CD) mesenchymal cells at E15.5 as assessed by RT-qPCR (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Pitx2 was elevated in Rab23-/- calvaria according to microarray analysis.
source: Our microarray analysis also showed that the transcription factor Pitx2 was elevated in Rab23-/- calvaria (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Pitx2 is a well-documented upstream regulator of Fgf10.
source: Pitx2 is a well-documented upstream regulator of Fgf10 and may act in a reciprocal regulatory loop with FGF10 during early organogenesis (Al Alam et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Pitx2 may act in a reciprocal regulatory loop with FGF10 during early organogenesis.
source: Pitx2 is a well-documented upstream regulator of Fgf10 and may act in a reciprocal regulatory loop with FGF10 during early organogenesis (Al Alam et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on prior literature.

claim: Pitx2 was overexpressed in Rab23-/- calvaria.
source: We found that Pitx2 was overexpressed both in the Rab23-/- calvaria and in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Pitx2 was overexpressed in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures.
source: We found that Pitx2 was overexpressed both in the Rab23-/- calvaria and in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Pitx2 overexpression was observed in Rab23-/- calvaria by whole-mount in situ hybridization in and surrounding the interparietal bone.
source: Pitx2 overexpression was further observed in Rab23-/- calvaria by whole-mount in situ hybridization in and surrounding the interparietal bone (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by whole-mount in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Fgfr1b expression was elevated in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutural mesenchymal tissue.
source: We assessed the expression of FGF10-specific receptors Fgfr1b, Fgfr2b, also Fgfr2c in Wt and Rab23-/- lambdoid sutural mesenchymal tissue. Our analysis showed elevated Fgfr1b expression and a non-significant upregulation of Fgfr2b in Rab23-/- samples (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Fgfr2b expression showed a non-significant upregulation in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutural mesenchymal tissue.
source: We assessed the expression of FGF10-specific receptors Fgfr1b, Fgfr2b, also Fgfr2c in Wt and Rab23-/- lambdoid sutural mesenchymal tissue. Our analysis showed elevated Fgfr1b expression and a non-significant upregulation of Fgfr2b in Rab23-/- samples (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Fgfr2c expression was unchanged in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutural mesenchymal tissue.
source: The expression of Fgfr2c was unchanged (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: FGFR1 protein levels were elevated in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures compared to Wt samples.
source: FGFR1 protein levels were found to be elevated in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures compared to Wt samples when analyzed by western blotting (Figure 2H,I) and by immunohistochemical staining (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 2H,I and immunohistochemical staining in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Exogenous FGF10 treatment on wild-type calvaria derived mesenchymal cells resulted in significant upregulation of Fgfr1b expression.
source: To test whether the upregulation of Fgfr1b and Fgfr2b expression was due to the high levels of FGF10 ligand present in the Rab23-/- lambdoid suture, we isolated E15.5 wild-type calvaria derived (CD) mesenchymal cells and treated them with exogenous FGF10 (250 ng/ml) for 3 hr. Fgfr1b and Fgfr2b expression levels were then assessed by RT-qPCR. We found a significant (p=0.05) upregulation of Fgfr1b expression and a slight upregulation of Fgfr2b expression in the cultured CD mesenchymal cells after exogenous FGF10 stimulation, indicating FGFR1B as a target of FGF10 in the calvarial mesenchyme (Figure 2J).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2J.

claim: Exogenous FGF10 treatment on wild-type calvaria derived mesenchymal cells resulted in a slight upregulation of Fgfr2b expression.
source: To test whether the upregulation of Fgfr1b and Fgfr2b expression was due to the high levels of FGF10 ligand present in the Rab23-/- lambdoid suture, we isolated E15.5 wild-type calvaria derived (CD) mesenchymal cells and treated them with exogenous FGF10 (250 ng/ml) for 3 hr. Fgfr1b and Fgfr2b expression levels were then assessed by RT-qPCR. We found a significant (p=0.05) upregulation of Fgfr1b expression and a slight upregulation of Fgfr2b expression in the cultured CD mesenchymal cells after exogenous FGF10 stimulation, indicating FGFR1B as a target of FGF10 in the calvarial mesenchyme (Figure 2J).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2J.

claim: FGFR1b is a target of FGF10 in the calvarial mesenchyme.
source: We found a significant (p=0.05) upregulation of Fgfr1b expression and a slight upregulation of Fgfr2b expression in the cultured CD mesenchymal cells after exogenous FGF10 stimulation, indicating FGFR1B as a target of FGF10 in the calvarial mesenchyme (Figure 2J).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing FGF10 induces Fgfr1b expression.

claim: FGF signaling activates MAPK signaling pathway subtypes pERK and p38 in suture morphogenesis and osteoblast differentiation.
source: FGF signaling has been shown to activate MAPK signaling pathway subtypes pERK and p38 in suture morphogenesis and osteoblast differentiation (Kyono et al., 2012; Pfaff et al., 2016; Figure 3A).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: In Rab23-/- lambdoid suture, p38 expression was decreased.
source: In Rab23-/- lambdoid suture, we found decreased p38 and elevated pERK1/2 and RUNX2 expressions compare to Wt samples (Figure 3B–G).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 3D,E.

claim: In Rab23-/- lambdoid suture, pERK1/2 expression was elevated.
source: In Rab23-/- lambdoid suture, we found decreased p38 and elevated pERK1/2 and RUNX2 expressions compare to Wt samples (Figure 3B–G).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: In Rab23-/- lambdoid suture, RUNX2 expression was elevated.
source: In Rab23-/- lambdoid suture, we found decreased p38 and elevated pERK1/2 and RUNX2 expressions compare to Wt samples (Figure 3B–G).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 3F,G.

claim: Exogenous FGF10 treatment on Rab23-/- calvaria derived mesenchymal cells resulted in significant upregulation of Runx2 expression at 2 and 4 hours.
source: To test whether the upregulation of RUNX2 expression was due to the high levels of FGF10 present in the Rab23-/- lambdoid suture, we isolated E15.5 Rab23-/- calvaria derived (CD) mesenchymal cells and treated them with exogenous FGF10 (500 ng/ml) for 2 and 4 hr. Runx2 expression levels were then assessed by RT-qPCR. We found a significant (p<0.05) upregulation of Runx2 expression at both time points compare to untreated samples, indicating that RUNX2 as a target of FGF10 in the calvarial mesenchyme (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: RUNX2 is a target of FGF10 in the calvarial mesenchyme.
source: We found a significant (p<0.05) upregulation of Runx2 expression at both time points compare to untreated samples, indicating that RUNX2 as a target of FGF10 in the calvarial mesenchyme (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing FGF10 induces Runx2 expression.

claim: ERK1/2 signaling regulates Hh and GLI expression.
source: Since ERK1/2 signaling regulates Hh and GLI expression, and RAB23 is a known negative regulator of Hh signaling (Eggenschwiler et al., 2001), we further assayed Hh, Gli1, Gli2, and Gli3 transcripts extracted from Wt and Rab23-/- lambdoid sutural mesenchyme at E15.5.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: A dramatic increase in the expression of Hh was detected in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutural mesenchyme at E15.5.
source: We detected a dramatic increase in the expression of Hh (Figure 3I) and Gli1 (Figure 3J), a sutural stem cell marker (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: A dramatic increase in the expression of Gli1 was detected in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutural mesenchyme at E15.5.
source: We detected a dramatic increase in the expression of Hh (Figure 3I) and Gli1 (Figure 3J), a sutural stem cell marker (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: GLI1 is a sutural stem cell marker.
source: We detected a dramatic increase in the expression of Hh (Figure 3I) and Gli1 (Figure 3J), a sutural stem cell marker (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Gli3 expression is not changed in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutural mesenchyme.
source: Although Gli3 expression is not changed, a functional change in the ratio of GLI3FL to GLI3R may still possible (Veistinen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data.

claim: A functional change in the ratio of GLI3FL to GLI3R may still be possible in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutural mesenchyme.
source: Although Gli3 expression is not changed, a functional change in the ratio of GLI3FL to GLI3R may still possible (Veistinen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on prior literature.

claim: No difference in pSMAD1/5/8 expression was found between Wt and Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures.
source: As TGFβ-superfamily members have also been shown to regulate suture patency (Kim et al., 1998; Komatsu et al., 2013; Pan et al., 2017), we assayed both pSMAD1/5/8 and pSMAD2/3 expressions but found no difference between Wt and mutant samples (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: No difference in pSMAD2/3 expression was found between Wt and Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures.
source: As TGFβ-superfamily members have also been shown to regulate suture patency (Kim et al., 1998; Komatsu et al., 2013; Pan et al., 2017), we assayed both pSMAD1/5/8 and pSMAD2/3 expressions but found no difference between Wt and mutant samples (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: FGF10-pERK1/2 signaling and RUNX2 regulate suture osteoprogenitor proliferation.
source: As FGF10-pERK1/2 signaling and RUNX2 are known to regulate suture osteoprogenitor proliferation (Kim et al., 1998; Qin et al., 2019), we assessed co-expression of EdU and RUNX2 in the WT and Rab23-/- lambdoid suture.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: EdU and RUNX2 co-localized in the osteogenic fronts indicating that the proliferating cells are osteoprogenitors.
source: EdU and RUNX2 co-localized in the osteogenic fronts indicating that the proliferating cells are osteoprogenitors (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical staining data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: EdU pulsed Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures showed more proliferating cells in the osteogenic fronts compared to Wt.
source: EdU pulsed Rab23-/- samples showed more proliferating cells in the osteogenic fronts compared to Wt (Figure 4C–H).
evidence: This is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 4C-H.

claim: Increased level of cell proliferation was observed in Rab23-/- derived mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) cells.
source: In addition, increased level of cell proliferation was observed in Rab23-/- derived mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) cells (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Rab23-/- calvaria derived cells had an elevated number of total cells at different passages (P1 to P3) when compared to Wt calvaria derived cells.
source: Rab23-/- calvaria derived cells also had an elevated number of total cells at different passages (P1 to P3) when compared to Wt calvaria derived cells (Figure 4J).
evidence: This is supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 4J.

claim: Increased proliferation in the sutures can result in a larger pool of osteoprogenitor cells and enhanced osteogenesis.
source: Increased proliferation in the sutures can result in a larger pool of osteoprogenitor cells and enhanced osteogenesis (Lana-Elola et al., 2007; Rice et al., 2003b).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: RAB23 is needed to repress proliferation in undifferentiated mesenchymal cells.
source: Taken together, this data shows that RAB23 is needed to repress proliferation in undifferentiated mesenchymal cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing increased proliferation in Rab23-/- cells.

claim: None of the untreated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures were rescued from fusion during in vitro culture.
source: None of the untreated Rab23-/- (n = 0/12) and 84.34% of U0126 treated Rab23-/- (n = 11/12) lambdoid sutures were rescued (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro culture data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: 84.34% of U0126 treated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures were rescued from fusion during in vitro culture.
source: None of the untreated Rab23-/- (n = 0/12) and 84.34% of U0126 treated Rab23-/- (n = 11/12) lambdoid sutures were rescued (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro culture data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: None of the Wt lambdoid sutures were fused during in vitro culture.
source: None of the Wt lambdoid sutures were fused (n = 0/12).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro culture data.

claim: Untreated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures underwent suture fusion by day 4 of in vitro culture at E17.5.
source: The same experiment (n = 4 in each genotype) was carried out with E17.5 samples and cultured for 4 days. Untreated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures underwent suture fusion by day 4, while U0126-treated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures remained patent during the culture period (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro culture data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: U0126-treated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures remained patent during 4 days of in vitro culture at E17.5.
source: The same experiment (n = 4 in each genotype) was carried out with E17.5 samples and cultured for 4 days. Untreated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures underwent suture fusion by day 4, while U0126-treated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures remained patent during the culture period (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro culture data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: U0126 had no effect on cell death in lambdoid sutural cells.
source: The effect of U0126 on sutural cells was also analyzed by cell death assay and no effect was observed in U0126-treated lambdoid sutural cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by apoptosis detection data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: U0126 treatment normalized the level of osteoprogenitor cell proliferation in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures.
source: U0126 treatment not only prevented suture fusion but it also normalized the level of osteoprogenitor cell proliferation (Figure 5D–G).
evidence: This is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 5D-G.

claim: U0126 treated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures exhibited reduced proliferation when compared to Rab23-/- controls after 24 hr of culture.
source: EdU incorporation revealed that U0126 treated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures (n = 8) exhibited reduced proliferation when compared to Rab23-/- controls (n = 8) (Figure 5D–G) and normalized it to Wt levels (n = 8) after 24 hr of culture (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: U0126 treatment normalized proliferation in Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures to Wt levels after 24 hr of culture.
source: EdU incorporation revealed that U0126 treated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures (n = 8) exhibited reduced proliferation when compared to Rab23-/- controls (n = 8) (Figure 5D–G) and normalized it to Wt levels (n = 8) after 24 hr of culture (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: The proliferation in all genotypes decreased over time during in vitro culture.
source: The proliferation in all genotypes decreased over time (Figure 5D–G).
evidence: This is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 5D-G.

claim: RAB23 regulates suture patency through a MAPK-MEK-ERK-driven mechanism.
source: This indicates that RAB23 regulates suture patency through a MAPK-MEK-ERK-driven mechanism.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that MEK inhibition rescues the Rab23-/- phenotype.

claim: After 6 hr of culture, the relative pERK1/2 levels were significantly reduced in U0126-treated Rab23-/- cells compared to untreated Rab23-/- cells.
source: After 6 hr of culture, the relative pERK1/2 levels were significantly reduced in U0126-treated Rab23-/- cells compare to untreated Rab23-/- cells. The downregulation of pERK1/2 continued in U0126-treated Rab23-/- cells at 24 and 48 hr of culture compare to the untreated Rab23-/- cells (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: The downregulation of pERK1/2 continued in U0126-treated Rab23-/- cells at 24 and 48 hr of culture compared to the untreated Rab23-/- cells.
source: After 6 hr of culture, the relative pERK1/2 levels were significantly reduced in U0126-treated Rab23-/- cells compare to untreated Rab23-/- cells. The downregulation of pERK1/2 continued in U0126-treated Rab23-/- cells at 24 and 48 hr of culture compare to the untreated Rab23-/- cells (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: RUNX2 expression significantly reduced only after 48 hr of U0126-treated Rab23-/- cells.
source: Whereas, RUNX2 expression significantly reduced only after 48 hr of U0126-treated Rab23-/- cells (Figure 6A,C).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6A,C.

claim: U0126-treated Rab23-/- cells showed gradual reduction of GLI1 expressions at 6 and 24 hr.
source: U0126-treated Rab23-/- cells showed gradual reduction of GLI1 expressions at 6 and 24 hr; however, it showed drastic reduction at 48 hr compared to untreated Rab23-/- cells (Figure 6A,D).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6A,D.

claim: U0126-treated Rab23-/- cells showed drastic reduction of GLI1 expression at 48 hr compared to untreated Rab23-/- cells.
source: U0126-treated Rab23-/- cells showed gradual reduction of GLI1 expressions at 6 and 24 hr; however, it showed drastic reduction at 48 hr compared to untreated Rab23-/- cells (Figure 6A,D).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6A,D.

claim: GLI1 expression was reduced in U0126 treated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures at 24 and 48 hr compared to untreated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures.
source: Further immunohistochemical expression of GLI1 was also found reduced in the U0126 treated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures at 24 and 48 hr compared to untreated Rab23-/- lambdoid sutures (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
